documents.title: Santa Clara University AI Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say 'the University does not have a university-wide policy for AI use across courses and curricula' and that 'faculty are expected to clearly communicate their policies', so the course-level stance is handed to instructors; the rest of the text is data, privacy, accuracy and research rules.
documents.summary: University-wide guidelines for faculty, staff, students and researchers on responsible AI use: procurement approval, data classification limits, verifying output, bias, IP, meeting assistants and research use. For coursework they leave the decision to faculty, add a caution about AI detectors, and point students to the Student Conduct Code.

units.why: The opening note calls the guidelines a work in progress that changes 'as the technology, the law and the University community usage evolves', so it is a statement that the policy is provisional: P54, informs, general.
units.anchor: as the technology, the law and the University community usage evolves

units.why: The purpose paragraph states the University is 'committed to actively and ethically engaging with artificial intelligence' in line with its mission; a framework preamble, so P56.
units.anchor: committed to actively and ethically engaging with artificial intelligence

units.why: The text says a working group 'has been convened' for administrative AI and a faculty/staff group will develop teaching guidance; this describes who made the guidance and how, so P84.
units.anchor: A University-wide cross-functional working group has been convened to specifically address AI in administrative areas
units.policy: A University-wide cross-functional working group has been convened to address AI in administrative areas, and a working group of faculty and staff will develop resources and guidelines around the use of AI in teaching.

units.why: The sentence says 'we must also use AI in a manner that is consistent with University policies and applicable laws', a duty to comply with law and existing policy: P77, must.
units.anchor: use AI in a manner that is consistent with University policies and applicable laws

units.why: Names 'the risk that an input could potentially become public' as a key attribute of AI tools; this is a privacy/data fact (P50), informs, not a rule itself.
units.anchor: the risk that an input could potentially become public

units.why: The second key attribute is 'the risk that the output may be biased, misleading, or inaccurate', the reason users must check output; P31, informs.
units.anchor: the risk that the output may be biased, misleading, or inaccurate

units.why: A listed risk about copyright of AI outputs ('may violate the IP rights of others'); P52 covers copyright and ownership of outputs, informs.
units.anchor: AI outputs may violate the IP rights of others, and might not themselves be protected

units.why: A listed risk that AI 'may produce decisions that are biased, discriminatory'; ethical and bias concerns fit P53, informs.
units.anchor: AI may produce decisions that are biased, discriminatory, or otherwise inconsistent with our policies

units.why: The Scope section says the Guidelines cover AI use by faculty, researchers, staff, students and others, which sets the scope and purpose of the framework: P56.
units.anchor: provide guidance on the use of AI tools by faculty, researchers, postdoctoral scholars, staff, students

units.why: Members are 'encouraged to regularly review the most recent version' of the Guidelines, a duty to keep up with current guidance: P102, should. Not P54 because it is addressed to users, not about the owner revising.
units.anchor: SCU community members are encouraged to regularly review the most recent version of these Guidelines

units.why: Requires TAR approval 'before purchasing (or acquiring for free) AI products' with cybersecurity, vendor-risk, legal and accessibility review; institutional approval of AI tools: P65, must.
units.anchor: obtain TAR approval before purchasing (or acquiring for free) AI products
units.policy: Complete the Technology Acquisition Request process and obtain TAR approval before purchasing (or acquiring for free) AI products or products that contain functions that rely on AI to operate.

units.why: 'Must not enter Level One Data or Level Two Data ... into any public or unapproved AI tool' bans putting personal and confidential data into AI tools: P50, must-not.
units.anchor: must not enter Level One Data or Level Two Data
units.policy: SCU community members must not enter Level One Data or Level Two Data (including personal information and confidential information) into any public or unapproved AI tool, except where the tool is approved for that data classification and use case through the TAR process.

units.why: Says members 'may enter Level Three Data into public AI tools' but that anything entered should be treated as public; this permits low-sensitivity data and warns about storage, P50, may.
units.anchor: may enter Level Three Data into public AI tools

units.why: Members 'must verify and validate each element of output' so a human audits AI content, because output can be inaccurate or fabricated: P31, must.
units.anchor: must verify and validate each element of output from AI tools

units.why: Users 'are responsible for any content published that includes AI-generated material', placing ownership on the user: P29, informs-as-duty (must).
units.anchor: are responsible for any content published that includes AI-generated material

units.why: Users 'should regularly stress test their AI tools' with simple and complex queries to learn limits; advice on probing tools to learn limitations: P93, should.
units.anchor: regularly stress test their AI tools

units.why: Members 'must consider' whether input and output cause 'disparate impact' based on protected classes: a bias check duty, P53, must.
units.anchor: must consider whether the data input into, and the output of, AI tools produces decisions

units.why: 'Do not rely on any output that is indicative of a potential bias' is a prohibition on using biased output; closest is P31 (verify and critically evaluate output), must-not.
units.anchor: Do not rely on any output that is indicative of a potential bias
units.fit_note: Concerns bias in output, not only factual accuracy, which P31 emphasizes.

units.why: 'Do not represent AI-generated content as solely your own work where credit or sourcing is required (e.g., academic submissions ... source coding)' demands acknowledgment where credit is required: P24, must-not.
units.anchor: Do not represent AI-generated content as solely your own work where credit or sourcing is
units.fit_note: Framed as a ban on misrepresenting authorship and conditioned on where credit or sourcing is required by instructor or policy, not an unconditional disclosure duty.

units.why: Where tools allow opting out of training, members 'are expected to exercise it and opt out of training'; a data-protection practice: P50, should.
units.anchor: expected to exercise it and opt out of training

units.why: Members 'are encouraged to use structured prompting frameworks' with roles, audience and context: advice on prompting, P93, should.
units.anchor: encouraged to use structured prompting frameworks with more tailored prompting

units.why: Says Information Services 'intends to publish a list of specific applications that have been vetted' and members are expected to use approved tools within scope; points users to the approved list: P92, informs.
units.anchor: The Information Services team intends to publish a list of specific applications that have been

units.why: AI meeting assistants 'should only' be Zoom AI Companion or TAR-approved tools; this limits meeting AI to approved tools, P92, should.
units.anchor: should only enable Zoom AI Companion and other TAR approved tools with contractual protections

units.why: Requires that 'all meeting participants are aware of and consent to the meeting being recorded / transcribed' before recording: consent for AI transcription, P86, must.
units.anchor: all meeting participants are aware of and consent to the meeting being recorded / transcribed
units.policy: Ensure that, at the beginning of the meeting, all meeting participants are aware of and consent to the meeting being recorded / transcribed, and begin recording only once all participants have consented.

units.why: 'If confidential data will be discussed, AI meeting assistants must not be used' is a data-protection ban: P50, must-not (P86 is about consent, not confidential content).
units.anchor: If confidential data will be discussed, AI meeting assistants must not be used

units.why: The coursework section grounds the rules in 'intellectual honesty and scholarly integrity' that could be undermined by AI content 'passed off as one's own work'; an integrity-culture rationale: P95, informs.
units.anchor: promote intellectual honesty and scholarly integrity, and deep, critical learning

units.why: The quoted Provost text says 'the University does not have a university-wide policy for AI use across courses', leaving it to faculty; so the university sets no rule and delegates: P04, informs.
units.anchor: the University does not have a university-wide policy for AI use across courses and curricula
units.policy: The University does not have a university-wide policy for AI use across courses and curricula; the faculty decide how and whether to integrate AI into their instruction.

units.why: The answer to how AI should be handled 'varies based on course, discipline, and industry contexts and related learning outcomes', tying decisions to outcomes: P83, informs.
units.anchor: varies based on course, discipline, and industry contexts and related learning outcomes objectives

units.why: Faculty weigh considerations 'to ensure that AI is facilitating and not replacing learning'; a learning-based criterion for faculty decisions, nearest P83.
units.anchor: ensure that AI is facilitating and not replacing learning
units.fit_note: States a criterion (AI facilitates, does not replace, learning) rather than naming specific learning objectives.

units.why: Faculty must weigh whether AI 'is accessible to students' when deciding to integrate it; accessibility consideration: P97, should.
units.anchor: is accessible to students
units.policy: Faculty weigh whether AI is accessible to students when determining how and whether to integrate it into their instruction.

units.why: 'Faculty are expected to clearly communicate their policies and rationales for AI use' in courses and assignments; the main requirement is communicating the policy: P09, must (rationales are also P66).
units.anchor: Faculty are expected to clearly communicate their policies and rationales for AI use in their
units.fit_note: Also expects instructors to share their rationales, which P66 covers.

units.why: Faculty 'expect students to maintain academic integrity and live up to student codes of conduct' in their learning; compliance with existing conduct rules: P77, must.
units.anchor: expect students to maintain academic integrity and live up to student codes of conduct

units.why: Notes AI detection tools carry 'risks of misidentification' with consequences in class; detectors are unreliable, so P39, informs.
units.anchor: there are risks of misidentification, which can have consequences in the classroom

units.why: 'AI detection should be treated as a guideline and not a grading metric' says detector output is supporting evidence, not proof: P69.
units.anchor: As with other plagiarism detection tools, AI detection should be treated as a guideline and

units.why: Instructors should 'include the use of these tools in any discussion with students around course policies', being transparent about detectors; explaining rules to students: P66, should.
units.anchor: include the use of these tools in any discussion with students around course policies
units.fit_note: Specifically asks instructors to tell students if and how detectors may be used.

units.why: Says clear 'escalation language, processes, and guidelines' in the event of detected plagiarism should be set at department level; a procedure-setting statement near P81, should.
units.anchor: Establishing clear escalation language, processes, and guidelines in the event of detected plagiarism, at the
units.fit_note: Asks departments to create escalation procedures, rather than telling instructors to follow a central reporting procedure.

units.why: Resources help faculty engage students on suspected misuse 'in an open and educational manner (especially given the number of false positives)'; an educative response: P68, should.
units.anchor: in an open and educational manner

units.why: Researchers 'should be transparent regarding its use, in describing methods, acknowledgements, or elsewhere'; research disclosure matches P24 (disclose AI use), should.
units.anchor: individuals who use AI in research should be transparent regarding its use
units.fit_note: Applies to research outputs rather than student submissions.

units.why: 'Researchers are responsible for the accuracy of any content created by AI' in research output; in the AI-and-research section so P62, must.
units.anchor: Researchers are responsible for the accuracy of any content created by AI that is included
units.fit_note: A research-specific accountability rule; P29 and P31 cover student work.

units.why: Researchers 'are expected to follow the policies of journals, funding agencies and professional societies', deferring to venue and funder rules: P62, must.
units.anchor: Researchers are expected to follow the policies of journals, funding agencies and professional societies

units.why: 'Researchers must avoid uploading ... unpublished research data or other confidential information into an unauthorized AI tool'; about data protection so P50 (not P62, which is about venue rules), must-not.
units.anchor: Researchers must avoid uploading, or using as input, any unpublished research data or other confidential

units.why: Researchers 'should comply with the expectations of their respective school, department and sub-discipline' plus journal and publisher rules; deferring to others' rules in research: P62, should.

units.why: Lists 'Citing AI tools used and clearly explaining their specific contributions rather than presenting AI-generated content as your own work' as documentation research may require: P24, should.
units.anchor: Citing AI tools used and clearly explaining their specific contributions

units.why: Suggests documenting verification by 'creating an audit trail by tracking the AI tools used, prompts, exact steps taken' to verify claims and citations; keeping logs: P26, should.
units.anchor: creating an audit trail by tracking the AI tools used, prompts, exact steps taken
units.fit_note: The audit trail is for verification of AI-generated citations in research.

units.why: 'All University research is subject to the University’s research integrity policies, such as the Policy on Research Misconduct', tying AI research use to existing policy: P77, informs.
units.anchor: All University research is subject to the University's research integrity policies

units.why: 'Students should review the policies relating to academic integrity in the Student Conduct Code'; students find and follow the applicable rules: P78, should.
units.anchor: Students should review the policies relating to academic integrity in the Student Conduct Code

documents.title: AI Syllabus Policy

tiers: AI permitted (graded specified assignments, ungraded work, self-study or case by case)
documents.summary: A library guide that helps faculty write an AI syllabus statement. It says there is no campus-wide policy, urges clarity, and gives sample wording for courses that allow AI and for courses that do not, plus parameters such as attribution, responsibility and data privacy.

units.why: After noting 'Santa Clara University currently does not have a campus wide AI policy', it says 'Faculty are encouraged to determine how AI tools and systems are utilized'; the instructor decides: P04, should.

units.why: Warns that 'by not having an AI statement in your syllabus you create ambiguous expectations'; urges a syllabus statement: P09, should.

units.why: The disclaimer says 'the library does not participate in syllabus creation or standards' and points to the Office of the Provost; names who owns syllabus standards: P80, informs.

units.why: Sample statement allowing AI on ungraded work 'because students can augment their learning outside of class' while still showing mastery without AI on graded work; AI to support learning: P12, may.

notes: Coder B. No CS department policy was collected; the School of Engineering pages include sample syllabus statements for COEN 11 and COEN 346 (computing courses) and ELEN/COEN 21, coded here as units of the school documents, not as course-layer documents. Several units use P04 for per-assignment permission and P10 is not used for 'prior permission' samples because those require permission rather than answering uncertainty.
